claim: The CRISPR/Cas9 system has been used to generate fluorescently labelled fusion proteins by homology-directed repair in a variety of species.
source: The CRISPR/Cas9 system has been used to generate fluorescently labelled fusion proteins by homology-directed repair in a variety of species.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work in the introduction section.

claim: There remains an urgent need for increased simplicity and efficiency of genome editing in research organisms.
source: Despite its revolutionary success, there remains an urgent need for increased simplicity and efficiency of genome editing in research organisms.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of the field based on the authors' assessment.

claim: A simplified, highly efficient, and precise strategy for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated endogenous protein tagging in medaka was established.
source: Here, we establish a simplified, highly efficient, and precise strategy for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated endogenous protein tagging in medaka (Oryzias latipes).
evidence: This is the main claim of the paper, supported by experimental data presented throughout.

claim: The approach uses a cloning-free method that relies on PCR-amplified donor fragments containing fluorescent reporter sequences flanked by short homology arms (30–40 bp).
source: We use a cloning-free approach that relies on PCR-amplified donor fragments containing the fluorescent reporter sequences flanked by short homology arms (30–40 bp), a synthetic single-guide RNA and Cas9 mRNA.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: Eight novel knock-in lines were generated with high efficiency of F0 targeting and germline transmission.
source: We generate eight novel knock-in lines with high efficiency of F0 targeting and germline transmission.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing the generation of multiple lines.

claim: Whole genome sequencing results reveal single-copy integration events only at the targeted loci.
source: Whole genome sequencing results reveal single-copy integration events only at the targeted loci.
evidence: This is supported by WGS data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The mScarlet-pcna line has the potential to serve as an organismal-wide label for proliferative zones and an endogenous cell cycle reporter.
source: In particular, we show that the mScarlet-pcna line has the potential to serve as an organismal-wide label for proliferative zones and an endogenous cell cycle reporter.
evidence: This is supported by experimental characterization of the mScarlet-pcna line.

claim: Molecular markers expressed at physiological levels are central to understanding cellular- and tissue-level dynamics during embryonic development.
source: These molecular markers expressed at physiological levels are central to our understanding of cellular- and tissue-level dynamics during embryonic development (Gibson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Researchers have utilized Cas9 and a programmed sgRNA to introduce a double strand break at a pre-defined genomic location.
source: To this end, researchers have utilized the Streptococcus pyogenes CRISPR-associated protein 9 (Cas9) and a programmed associated single-guide RNA (sgRNA) to introduce a double strand break (DSB) at a pre-defined genomic location (Jinek et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the foundational CRISPR paper.

claim: Providing DNA repair donors with homology arms that match those of the targeted locus can lead to integration of donor constructs containing fluorescent reporter sequences by homology-directed repair.
source: Cell DNA repair mechanisms are triggered by the DSB and it has been shown that providing DNA repair donors with homology arms that match those of the targeted locus can lead to integration of the donor constructs containing fluorescent reporter sequences in the genome by the process of homology-directed repair (HDR) (Danner et al., 2017; Jasin and Haber, 2016; Ceccaldi et al., 2016; Lisby and Rothstein, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on HDR mechanisms.

claim: HDR mediated precise single-copy KI efficiencies in vertebrate models can still be low and the process of generating KI lines remains cumbersome and time consuming.
source: Despite its success, HDR mediated precise single-copy KI efficiencies in vertebrate models can still be low and the process of generating KI lines remains cumbersome and time consuming.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of the field.

claim: Recent reports have improved the methodology by using 5′ biotinylated long homology arms that prevent concatemerization of the injected dsDNA.
source: Recent reports have improved the methodology by the usage of 5′ biotinylated long homology arms that prevent concatemerization of the injected dsDNA (Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018) or by linking the repair donor to the Cas9 protein (Gu et al., 2018; Savic et al., 2018; Carlson-Stevermer et al., 2017; Aird et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent methodological improvements.

claim: Repair donors with shorter homology arms in combination with in vivo linearization of the donor plasmid have been shown to mediate efficient knock-ins in zebrafish and in mammalian cells.
source: In addition, repair donors with shorter homology arms in combination with in vivo linearization of the donor plasmid have been shown to mediate efficient knock-ins in zebrafish and in mammalian cells (Wierson et al., 2020; Hisano et al., 2015; Cristea et al., 2013; Yao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The approach relies on the use of biotinylated PCR-amplified donor fragments that contain the fluorescent reporter sequences flanked by short homology arms (30–40 bp), by-passing the need for cloning or in vivo linearization.
source: Our approach relies on the use of biotinylated PCR-amplified donor fragments that contain the fluorescent reporter sequences flanked by short homology arms (30–40 bp), by-passing the need for cloning or in vivo linearization.
evidence: This describes the methodology developed in this study.

claim: Whole genome sequencing with high coverage in conjunction with Sanger sequencing of edited loci provides strong evidence for precise single-copy integration events only at the desired loci.
source: By utilizing whole genome sequencing (WGS) with high coverage in conjunction with Sanger sequencing of edited loci, we provide strong evidence for precise single-copy integration events only at the desired loci.
evidence: This is supported by WGS and Sanger sequencing data.

claim: The KI lines allow recording of cellular processes, such as intra-cellular trafficking and stress granule formation in 4D during embryonic development.
source: In addition to generating an endogenous ubiquitous nuclear label and novel tissue-specific reporters, the KI lines allow us to record cellular processes, such as intra-cellular trafficking and stress granule formation in 4D during embryonic development, significantly expanding the genetic toolkit available in medaka.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data of the generated lines.

claim: The endogenous mScarlet-pcna KI serves as a bona fide proliferative cell label and an endogenous cell cycle reporter.
source: Finally, we provide proof-of-principle evidence that the endogenous mScarlet-pcna KI we generate serves as a bona fide proliferative cell label and an endogenous cell cycle reporter, with broad application potential in a vertebrate model system.
evidence: This is supported by experimental characterization of the mScarlet-pcna line.

claim: Biotinylated 5′ ends were used to prevent in vivo concatemerization of DNA.
source: In addition, biotinylated 5′ ends were used to prevent in vivo concatemerization of DNA (Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a methodological detail supported by citation.

claim: A streptavidin-tagged Cas9 (Cas9-mSA) was used with the goal of enhancing its binding to the biotinylated repair donor constructs.
source: We used a streptavidin-tagged Cas9 (Cas9-mSA), with the goal of enhancing its binding to the biotinylated repair donor constructs (Gu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a methodological detail supported by citation.

claim: The approach by-passes the need for cloning, as the short homology arms are added during PCR amplification.
source: This approach by-passes the need for cloning, as the short homology arms are added during PCR amplification.
evidence: This describes a key advantage of the methodology.

claim: Given a linear PCR repair donor is used, there is no need for a second gRNA for in vivo plasmid linearization.
source: Also, given a linear PCR repair donor is used, there is no need for a second gRNA for in vivo plasmid linearization (Hoshijima et al., 2016; Shin et al., 2014; Zu et al., 2013; Yao et al., 2017; Cristea et al., 2013; Auer et al., 2014; Hisano et al., 2015; Li et al., 2019; Wierson et al., 2020; Kimura et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes another advantage of the methodology, supported by citations.

claim: Eight genes were targeted with a variety of fluorescent proteins.
source: We targeted a list of eight genes with a variety of fluorescent proteins (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Supplementary files 3a-d and 4), both N and C terminus tags were attempted (a list of all genomic loci targeted can be found in Supplementary file 3a).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and supplementary files.

claim: Targeting efficiency in F0 ranged from 11% to 59% of embryos showing mosaic expression.
source: Targeting efficiency in F0 ranged from 11% to 59% of embryos showing mosaic expression (Supplementary files 3a and 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in supplementary files.

claim: Control injections with the actb sgRNA, Cas9-mSA mRNA, and the donor eGFP construct without homology arms showed no evidence of eGFP-positive cell clones in F0.
source: Control injections with the actb sgRNA, Cas9-mSA mRNA, and the donor eGFP construct without homology arms showed no evidence of eGFP-positive cell clones in F0 (Supplementary file 3a), while the same construct with homology arms resulted in 39% of surviving injected embryos showing mosaic expression of eGFP (Supplementary files 3a and 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental control data.

claim: The germline transmission efficiency of fluorescent F0 fish ranged from 25% to 100% for the different targeted loci.
source: The germline transmission efficiency of fluorescent F0 fish ranged from 25% to 100% for the different targeted loci (Supplementary files 3a and 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in supplementary files.

claim: For F0 adults with germline transmission, the percentage of positive F1 embryos ranged between 6.6% (2/30) and 50% (25/50).
source: For F0 adults with germline transmission, the percentage of positive F1 embryos ranged between 6.6% (2/30) and 50% (25/50).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: Eight stable KI lines were established using this method.
source: Using this method, we were able to establish eight stable KI lines.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: A single injection round was sufficient to generate a KI line for most targeted loci (7/8).
source: Importantly, a single injection round was sufficient to generate a KI line for most targeted loci (7/8; Supplementary files 3a-f and 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in supplementary files.

claim: The actb-eGFP tag was embryonic lethal.
source: As previously reported, the actb-eGFP tag was embryonic lethal (Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018) and we could not obtain a KI line for that locus.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work and experimental observation.

claim: Initial comparison between different Cas9 designs indicates comparable efficiencies of KI insertions in F0s, irrespective of whether a streptavidin tag was included.
source: We also performed an initial comparison (using fluorescent screening in F0) between different Cas9 designs, that is, with and without mSA. Our results indicate comparable efficiencies of KI insertions in F0s, irrespective of whether a streptavidin tag was included (Supplementary file 3g).
evidence: This is supported by experimental comparison data.

claim: Highly efficient targeting of endogenous loci with large inserts (~800 bp) is obtained in medaka using the simplified KI approach.
source: Combined, our results provide evidence that highly efficient targeting of endogenous loci with large inserts (~800 bp) is obtained in medaka using the simplified KI approach presented here (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data.

claim: The protocol is rapid and simple-to-implement, as it relies on a PCR-amplified repair construct and hence alleviates the need for any additional cloning or in vivo plasmid linearization.
source: In addition to being highly efficient, this protocol is rapid and simple-to-implement, as it relies on a PCR-amplified repair construct and hence  alleviates the need for any additional cloning or in vivo plasmid linearization (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes advantages of the methodology.

claim: Concatemerization of inserts or off-target integrations could occur after foreign DNA delivery and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated DSBs.
source: It is possible that either concatemerization of inserts or off-target integrations could occur after foreign DNA delivery and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated DSBs (Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018; Doench et al., 2016; Fu et al., 2013; Paix et al., 2017a, Won and Dawid, 2017; Yan et al., 2013; Hackett et al., 2007; Wierson et al., 2020; Auer et al., 2014; Shin et al., 2014; Winkler et al., 1991; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Kimura et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work documenting these issues.

claim: Next generation WGS with high coverage was performed on three KI lines: eGFP-cbx1b, mScarlet-pcna, and mNeonGreen-myosinhc.
source: To identify off-target insertions genome wide and verify single-copy integration we performed next generation WGS with high coverage (for details of WGS, see Materials and methods) on three KI lines (Figure 1B–D): eGFP-cbx1b, mScarlet-pcna, and mNeonGreen-myosinhc.
evidence: This describes the validation approach used.

claim: For the eGFP-cbx1b KI line, paired-end eGFP reads were only identified anchored to the endogenous cbx1b locus and nowhere else in the genome.
source: For the eGFP-cbx1b KI line, we could only identify paired-end eGFP reads anchored to the endogenous cbx1b locus and nowhere else in the genome (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by WGS data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In the mScarlet-pcna line, mScarlet reads only mapped to the endogenous pcna locus.
source: Likewise, in the mScarlet-pcna line, mScarlet reads only mapped to the endogenous pcna locus (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by WGS data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: For the mNeonGreen-myosinhc line, mNeonGreen sequences mapped to the myosinhc locus.
source: For the mNeonGreen-myosinhc line, mNeonGreen sequences mapped to the myosinhc locus (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C), but paired-end analysis yielded a second, weakly supported partial insertion of mNeonGreen at an intronic region in the edf1 gene.
evidence: This is supported by WGS data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The second insertion in the mNeonGreen-myosinhc line could not be confirmed by subsequent PCR and hence it remains unclear whether this is a false-positive prediction or a rare insertion of very low frequency.
source: We were not able to confirm the latter insertion by subsequent PCR and hence it remains unclear whether this a false-positive prediction or a rare insertion of very low frequency.
evidence: This is based on experimental validation attempts.

claim: The WGS results provide strong evidence that the method results in single-copy insertions only at the targeted locus.
source: Combined, the WGS results therefore provide strong evidence that the method we report results in single-copy insertions only at the targeted locus.
evidence: This is supported by WGS data from three lines.

claim: Genotyping F1 adults followed by Sanger sequencing confirmed the generation of single-copy in-frame fusion proteins in seven lines.
source: In addition to WGS, genotyping F1 adults followed by Sanger sequencing confirmed the generation of single-copy in-frame fusion proteins in the eGFP-cbx1b, mGreenLantern-cbx1b, mScarlet-pcna, mNeonGreen-myosinhc, cdh2-eGFP, mapre1b-mScarlet, and eGFP-rab11a lines (Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Supplementary file 3f, and Materials and methods).
evidence: This is supported by Sanger sequencing data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Only 2/14 Sanger sequenced junctions showed evidence of imprecise repair following HDR.
source: Only 2/14 Sanger sequenced junctions showed evidence of imprecise repair following HDR, one of which was a partial duplication within the 5′ homology arm, 22 basepairs upstream of the start codon while the other showed a partial duplication within the 3′ homology arm four basepairs after the stop codon (for details see Materials and methods), in both cases the coding sequence of the targeted genes is unaffected.
evidence: This is supported by Sanger sequencing data.

claim: The method shows high precision and specificity enabling the rapid generation of endogenously tagged alleles in a vertebrate model.
source: Overall, the method we present here shows high precision and specificity enabling the rapid generation of endogenously tagged alleles in a vertebrate model.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the validation data.

claim: The cbx1b locus was targeted with eGFP and mGreenLantern to generate a ubiquitously expressed nuclear label reporter line.
source: To generate a ubiquitously expressed nuclear label reporter line, we targeted the cbx1b (Chromobox protein homolog) locus with eGFP and mGreenLantern (mGL).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach for generating a specific line.

claim: Cbx1b is a member of the chromobox DNA-binding protein family and is a known component of heterochromatin that is expressed ubiquitously.
source: Cbx1b is a member of the chromobox DNA-binding protein family and is a known component of heterochromatin that is expressed ubiquitously (Lomberk et al., 2006; Nielsen et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Chromobox proteins are involved in several important functions within the nucleus, such as transcription, nuclear architecture, and DNA damage response.
source: Chromobox proteins are involved in several important functions within the nucleus, such as transcription, nuclear architecture, and DNA damage response (Luijsterburg et al., 2009; Gilmore et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Two KI lines eGFP-cbx1b and mGL-cbx1b were generated by targeting either eGFP or mGL to the N-terminus of the cbx1b coding sequence in medaka.
source: We generated two KI lines eGFP-cbx1b and mGL-cbx1b by targeting either eGFP or mGL to the N-terminus of the cbx1b coding sequence in medaka.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach.

claim: The eGFP-cbx1b and mGL-cbx1b lines express the fluorescent reporter in all nuclei of every tissue examined, and serve as endogenous ubiquitous nuclear labels in teleosts.
source: The resulting lines express the fluorescent reporter in all nuclei of every tissue examined, and serve as endogenous ubiquitous nuclear labels in teleosts (Figure 1B and Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2, and Video 1, n > 10 embryos).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in multiple figures and videos.

claim: The pcna locus was targeted to generate a mScarlet-pcna fusion protein with the goal of generating an endogenous cell cycle reporter.
source: With the goal of generating an endogenous cell cycle reporter, we targeted the pcna (proliferating cell nuclear antigen) locus to generate a mScarlet-pcna fusion protein.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach.

claim: Pcna is an essential protein regulator of DNA replication and integrity in eukaryotic cells.
source: Pcna is an essential protein regulator of DNA replication and integrity in eukaryotic cells (Moldovan et al., 2007; Maga and Hubscher, 2003; Mailand et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Cells that exit the cell cycle express very low levels of Pcna.
source: It has been previously shown that cells that exit the cell cycle, for example post-mitotic differentiated cell types, express very low levels of Pcna (Zerjatke et al., 2017; Thacker et al., 2003; Yamaguchi et al., 1995; Buttitta et al., 2010; Alunni et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Pcna has been utilized as a highly conserved marker for proliferating cells.
source: This has led researchers to utilize Pcna as a highly conserved marker for proliferating cells (Zerjatke et al., 2017; Barr et al., 2016; Leonhardt et al., 2000; Leung et al., 2011; Piwko et al., 2010; Alunni et al., 2010; Thacker et al., 2003; Santos et al., 2015; Held et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The appearance of nuclear speckles of Pcna within the nucleus is a hallmark of cells in late S phase of the cell cycle.
source: In addition to being a specific label for cycling cells, the appearance of nuclear speckles of Pcna within the nucleus is a hallmark of cells in late S phase of the cell cycle (Zerjatke et al., 2017; Barr et al., 2016; Leonhardt et al., 2000; Leung et al., 2011; Piwko et al., 2010; Santos et al., 2015; Held et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Endogenously tagged Pcna has been used in mammalian cell lines to dynamically score all the different cell cycle phases.
source: More recently, endogenously tagged Pcna has been used in mammalian cell lines to dynamically score all the different cell cycle phases (Zerjatke et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The first exon of pcna was targeted with mScarlet with high efficiency (28% mosaic expression in F0s, and 50% germline transmission) to generate the mScarlet-pcna KI line.
source: We targeted the first exon of pcna with mScarlet with high efficiency (28% mosaic expression in F0s, and 50% germline transmission) and generated the mScarlet-pcna KI line (Figure 1C and Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and imaging.

claim: mScarlet-Pcna-positive cells were detected within the epidermis, specifically in supra-basal epidermal cells in stage 40 medaka embryos.
source: Using stage 40 medaka embryos, we detected mScarlet-Pcna-positive cells within the epidermis, specifically in supra-basal epidermal cells (Figure 2B, n = 10 embryos).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A subset of epidermal cells showed nuclear speckles of mScarlet-Pcna that likely represent replication foci and are a characteristic marker for late S phase.
source: A subset of these cells showed nuclear speckles of mScarlet-Pcna that likely represent replication foci and are a characteristic marker for late S phase (Figure 2B, yellow arrowheads).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data and inference based on known Pcna behavior.

claim: Rab11a is a small GTPase and known marker of intra-cellular trafficking organelles in vertebrates.
source: To generate a reporter line allowing monitoring subcellular trafficking of endosomes and exosomes, we targeted Rab11a (Ras-Related Protein), a small GTPase and known marker of intra-cellular trafficking organelles in vertebrates (Welz et al., 2014; Cullen and Steinberg, 2018; Stenmark, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: An N-terminus tagged eGFP-rab11a fusion protein was generated that shows punctate intra-cellular signal most likely corresponding to trafficking organelles.
source: We generated an N-terminus tagged eGFP-rab11a fusion protein that shows punctate intra-cellular signal most likely corresponding to trafficking organelles (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 3, and Videos 2–4, n = 4 embryos).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: High levels of eGFP-rab11a were detected in cells of the spinal cord and in neuromasts of the lateral line.
source: As a proof of principle, we detected high levels of eGFP-rab11a in cells of the spinal cord (Figure 2C, yellow arrowhead) and in neuromasts of the lateral line (Figure 2C, magenta arrowhead, Figure 2—figure supplement 3, and Video 4, n = 6 embryos).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: Dynamics of what appear to be intra-cellular organelle trafficking were observed in vivo in individual skin epithelial cells and in the caudal fin region of developing medaka embryos using the eGFP-rab11a KI line.
source: Using the eGFP-rab11a KI line, we were also able to observe dynamics of what appear to be intra-cellular organelle trafficking in vivo both in individual skin epithelial cells in the mid-trunk region and in the caudal fin region of developing medaka embryos (Videos 2 and 3, n = 4 embryos) providing initial evidence of the utility of this line as a possible subcellular trafficking marker in medaka.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in videos.

claim: A g3b1-eGFP KI line was generated by targeting eGFP to the 11th exon of the medaka g3bp1 gene.
source: We were able to generate a g3b1-eGFP KI line by targeting eGFP to the 11th exon of the medaka g3bp1 gene.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach.

claim: G3bp1 is a DNA/RNA-binding protein and an initiating factor involved in stress granule formation.
source: G3bp1 (GTPase activating protein SH3-domain-binding protein) is a DNA/RNA-binding protein and an initiating factor involved in stress granule formation (Irvine et al., 2004; Yang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Stress granules are non-membrane bound cell compartments, which form under cellular stress and accumulate non-translating mRNA and protein complexes, and play an important role in cellular protection by regulating mRNA translation and stability.
source: Stress granules are non-membrane bound cell compartments, which form under cellular stress and accumulate non-translating mRNA and protein complexes, and play an important role in cellular protection by regulating mRNA translation and stability (Decker and Parker, 2012; Protter and Parker, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Under normal conditions G3bp1-eGFP is expressed in the cytoplasm.
source: Under normal conditions G3bp1-eGFP is expressed in the cytoplasm (Figure 2F, Video 5, n = 8 embryos) but upon stress (temperature shock), we observe that the protein changes its localization and accumulates in cytoplasmic foci corresponding to forming stress granules (Figure 2F', yellow arrowheads, Video 5, n = 8 embryos).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: Upon stress (temperature shock), G3bp1-eGFP changes its localization and accumulates in cytoplasmic foci corresponding to forming stress granules.
source: Under normal conditions G3bp1-eGFP is expressed in the cytoplasm (Figure 2F, Video 5, n = 8 embryos) but upon stress (temperature shock), we observe that the protein changes its localization and accumulates in cytoplasmic foci corresponding to forming stress granules (Figure 2F', yellow arrowheads, Video 5, n = 8 embryos).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: The observed changes in G3bp1 localization in response to stress are consistent with previous reports in other organisms.
source: This is consistent with previous reports showing similar changes in the localization of G3bp1 in response to stress in a number of organisms (Guarino et al., 2019; Wheeler et al., 2016; Kuo et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The g3bp1-eGFP line has the potential to serve as a real-time in vivo reporter for the dynamics of stress granules formation in a vertebrate model.
source: The initial characterization of the g3bp1-eGFP line shows its potential to serve as a real-time in vivo reporter for the dynamics of stress granules formation in a vertebrate model.
evidence: This is an inference based on the characterization data.

claim: Muscular myosin heavy chain was targeted with mNeonGreen to label muscle cells.
source: To label muscle cells, we targeted muscular myosin heavy chain with mNeonGreen (mNG).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach.

claim: Myosins are a highly conserved class of motor proteins implicated in actin microfilament reorganization and movement.
source: Myosins are a highly conserved class of motor proteins implicated in actin microfilament reorganization and movement (Sellers, 2000; Hartman and Spudich, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: An N-terminus fusion of mNG-myosinhc KI was generated that exclusively labels muscle cells.
source: We generated an N-terminus fusion of mNG-myosinhc KI that exclusively labels muscle cells (Figure 1D and Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 4, n > 10 embryos).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in figures.

claim: In the medaka myotome, chains of individual sarcomeres were observed with mNG-myosinhc labeling the Myosin A band inside each sarcomere.
source: In the medaka myotome, we were able to observe mNG-myosinhc chains of individual sarcomeres (A-bands separated by the I-bands), indicating that tagged Myosinhc is incorporated correctly in muscle fibers (Taylor et al., 2015; Loison et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data and citations to prior work on sarcomere structure.

claim: The mNG-myosinhc line enables the in vivo recording of endogenous Myosinhc dynamics during muscle growth for the first time in a vertebrate model.
source: We use this line to record the endogenous dynamics of Myosinhc during muscle growth in vivo for the first time to the best of our knowledge, in a vertebrate model (Video 6, n = 9 embryos).
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in videos.

claim: Cadherins are a highly conserved class of transmembrane proteins that are essential components of cell–cell adhesion and are expressed on cellular membranes.
source: Cadherins are a highly conserved class of transmembrane proteins that are essential components of cell–cell adhesion and are thus expressed on cellular membranes (Leckband and de Rooij, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: A large number of cadherin genes exist in vertebrates where they exhibit tissue-specific expression patterns and are implicated in various developmental processes.
source: A large number of cadherin genes exist in vertebrates where they exhibit tissue-specific expression patterns and are implicated in various developmental processes (Halbleib and Nelson, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The C-terminus of medaka cadherin 2 (cdh2, n-cadherin) was tagged with eGFP.
source: We decided to tag the C-terminus of medaka cadherin 2 (cdh2, n-cadherin) with eGFP.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach.

claim: cdh2 is known to be expressed primarily in neuronal tissues in a number of vertebrates.
source: cdh2 is known to be expressed primarily in neuronal tissues in a number of vertebrates (Harrington et al., 2007; Suzuki and Takeichi, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The cdh2-eGFP KI line shows cellular membrane expression in a variety of neuronal and non-neuronal tissues including the spinal cord, the eye, and the notochord.
source: The cdh2-eGFP KI line shows cellular membrane expression in a variety of neuronal and non-neuronal tissues including the spinal cord, the eye, and the notochord (Figure 2E, n = 5 embryos) and neuromasts of the lateral line (Figure 2—figure supplement 3, n = 5 embryos, Video 7,  n = 3 embryos), in addition to the developing heart (data not shown) (Chopra et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: The high expression of cdh2 in both differentiated notochord cell types has not been previously reported in medaka but is not unexpected as this tissue experiences a high level of mechanical stress and requires strong cell–cell adhesion.
source: The high expression of cdh2 in both differentiated notochord cell types (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 3) has not been previously reported in medaka but is not unexpected as this tissue experiences a high level of mechanical stress and requires strong cell–cell adhesion (Lim et al., 2017; Adams et al., 1990; Garcia et al., 2017; Seleit et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data and citations to prior work on notochord mechanics.

claim: The cdh2-eGFP KI can be used to study dynamics of n-cadherin distribution in vivo during vertebrate embryogenesis.
source: The cdh2-eGFP KI can be used to study dynamics of n-cadherin distribution in vivo during vertebrate embryogenesis (Video 8, n = 2 embryos).
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in videos.

claim: Microtubule plus-end binding proteins are conserved regulators of microtubule dynamics, acting as a scaffold to recruit several additional proteins to ensure essential cell functions such as cell polarity, intra-cellular transport, and mitosis.
source: Microtubule plus-end binding proteins are conserved regulators of microtubule dynamics, acting as a scaffold to recruit several additional proteins to ensure essential cell functions such as cell polarity, intra-cellular transport, and mitosis (Nehlig et al., 2017; Tirnauer and Bierer, 2000; Galjart, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The microtubule plus-end binding protein mapre1b (eb1) was successfully targeted, generating a C-terminal fusion protein with mScarlet.
source: We successfully targeted the microtubule plus-end binding protein mapre1b (eb1), generating a C-terminal fusion protein with mScarlet.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach.

claim: mapre1b-mScarlet is widely expressed in medaka embryos: epithelial cells, muscle cells, the notochord, and neuromasts all show mapre1b-mScarlet expression, with the highest level of expression occurring in the spinal cord.
source: mapre1b-mScarlet is widely expressed in medaka embryos: epithelial cells, muscle cells, the notochord, and neuromasts all show mapre1b-mScarlet expression (Figure 2G, Video 9, n = 5 embryos), the highest level of expression occurs in the spinal cord (Figure 2G, yellow arrowhead).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: Microtubule dynamics in the spinal cord of living embryos were recorded using the mapre1b-mScarlet line.
source: We were also able to record microtubule dynamics in the spinal cord of living embryos (Video 10, n = 5 embryos) highlighting the utility of this line for exploring the dynamics of microtubules in vivo during development.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in videos.

claim: The novel mScarlet-pcna line can act as an organismal-wide bona fide marker for the location of proliferative cells within any tissue or organ of interest.
source: We reasoned that the novel mScarlet-pcna line can act as an organismal-wide bona fide marker for the location of proliferative cells within any tissue or organ of interest.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the properties of Pcna.

claim: Double transgenic animals were generated with eGFP-cbx1b as a ubiquitous nuclear marker and mScarlet-pcna as a label for cycling cells.
source: We therefore decided to generate double transgenic animals with eGFP-cbx1b as a ubiquitous nuclear marker and mScarlet-pcna as a label for cycling cells (Figure 3).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach.

claim: Neuromasts are small rosette shaped sensory organs located on the surface of teleost fish that sense the direction of water flow and relay the information back to the central nervous system.
source: Neuromasts are small rosette shaped sensory organs located on the surface of teleost fish that sense the direction of water flow and relay the information back to the central nervous system (Seleit et al., 2017a; Romero-Carvajal et al., 2015; Jones and Corwin, 1993; Wada et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Neuromasts consist of four cell types: differentiated hair cells (HCs) in the very centre, underlying support cells (SCs), a ring of mantle cells (MCs), and neuromast border cells (nBCs).
source: They consist of four cell types: differentiated hair cells (HCs) in the very centre, underlying support cells (SCs), a ring of mantle cells (MCs), and neuromast border cells (nBCs) (Seleit et al., 2017b; Dufourcq et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Previous work in medaka has established MCs to be the true life-long neural stem cells within mature neuromast organs.
source: Previous work in medaka has established MCs to be the true life-long neural stem cells within mature neuromast organs (Seleit et al., 2017b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: eGFP-cbx1b labels all neural cells within a mature neuromast organ (HCs, SCs, and MCs).
source: While the eGFP-cbx1b labels all neural cells within a mature neuromast organ (HCs, SCs, and MCs) (Figure 3A), mScarlet-pcna expression matches the previously reported location of proliferative MCs (Seleit et al., 2017b; Figure 3A'–A'', white arrowhead).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: mScarlet-pcna expression matches the previously reported location of proliferative MCs in neuromasts.
source: While the eGFP-cbx1b labels all neural cells within a mature neuromast organ (HCs, SCs, and MCs) (Figure 3A), mScarlet-pcna expression matches the previously reported location of proliferative MCs (Seleit et al., 2017b; Figure 3A'–A'', white arrowhead).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A' and citation to prior work.

claim: Neither the differentiated HCs nor the SCs directly surrounding them show evidence of Pcna expression in mature neuromast organs under homeostatic conditions in medaka.
source: Neither the differentiated HCs nor the SCs directly surrounding them show evidence of Pcna expression in mature neuromast organs under homeostatic conditions in medaka (Figure 3A–A'', n = 10 neuromast organs).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The results validate the utility of mScarlet-pcna as an in vivo marker of proliferative cells.
source: Our results validate the utility of mScarlet-pcna as an in vivo marker of proliferative cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the neuromast data.

claim: nBCs are induced to form from epithelial cells that come into contact with neuromast precursors during organ formation and these induced cells become the stem cell niche of mature neuromast organs.
source: Previous work has shown that nBCs are induced to form from epithelial cells that come into contact with neuromast precursors during organ formation and that these induced cells become the stem cell niche of mature neuromast organs (Seleit et al., 2017b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: nBCs (4/42) in late S phase of the cell cycle were observed in mature neuromast organs, as evident by the presence of nuclear speckles.
source: Utilizing the mScarlet-pcna line we were able to observe nBCs (4/42) in late S phase of the cell cycle, as evident by the presence of nuclear speckles, in mature neuromast organs (Figure 3A'–A'', yellow arrowheads).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A'.

claim: The observation of nBCs in late S phase provides direct evidence that nBCs retain the ability to divide and are thus not post-mitotic cells.
source: This provides direct evidence that nBCs retain the ability to divide and are thus not post-mitotic cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of cycling nBCs.

claim: Proliferative cells in the optic tectum of medaka are located at the lateral, caudal, and medial edge of the tectum in a crescent-like topology.
source: We show that proliferative cells in the optic tectum of medaka are located at the lateral, caudal, and medial edge of the tectum in a crescent-like topology (Figure 3B–B'', n = 4 embryos).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: mScarlet-pcna expression is graded in the optic tectum, with the more central cells gradually losing expression of Pcna.
source: Moreover, mScarlet-pcna expression is graded, with the more central cells gradually losing expression of Pcna (Figure 3B').
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3B'.

claim: The observed proliferation pattern in the optic tectum is in line with previous histological findings using BrdU/IdU stainings in similarly staged medaka embryos.
source: This is in line with previous histological findings using BrdU/IdU stainings in similarly staged medaka embryos (Nguyen et al., 1999; Alunni et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Cells located proximally in the developing pectoral fin expressed the highest levels of mScarlet-pcna, with mScarlet-pcna expression decreasing gradually along the proximo-distal axis.
source: We found that cells located proximally expressed the highest levels of mScarlet-pcna, with mScarlet-pcna expression decreasing gradually along the proximo-distal axis (Figure 3C').
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3C'.

claim: The proliferation pattern in the pectoral fin has not been previously reported and provides evidence that the differentiation axis of the pectoral fin is spatially organized from proximal to distal in medaka.
source: To the best of our knowledge this proliferation pattern has not been previously reported and our data provide evidence that the differentiation axis of the pectoral fin is spatially organized from proximal to distal in medaka.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed proliferation pattern.

claim: Proliferative cells are present in the spinal cord of stage 40 medaka embryos, and these mScarlet-Pcna-positive cells occur in clusters preferentially located on the dorsal side of the spine.
source: Lastly, we reveal that proliferative cells are present in the spinal cord of stage 40 medaka embryos, a finding that has not been previously reported, and we show that these mScarlet-Pcna-positive cells occur in clusters preferentially located on the dorsal side of the spine (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, n = 4 embryos).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The mScarlet-pcna line acts as a stable label of proliferative cells and can be used to uncover the location of proliferation zones in vivo within organs or tissues of interest in medaka.
source: The newly developed mScarlet-pcna line therefore acts as a stable label of proliferative cells and as such can be used to uncover the location of proliferation zones in vivo within organs or tissues of interest in medaka.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the characterization data.

claim: Endogenously tagged Pcna can be used to determine all cell cycle phases based on the fact that both the levels and dynamic distribution of Pcna show reproducible characteristics in each phase of the cell cycle.
source: In addition to its use as a marker for cells in S phase, it has been shown that endogenously tagged Pcna can be used to determine all other cell cycle phases. This is based on the fact that both the levels and dynamic distribution of Pcna show reproducible characteristics in each phase of the cell cycle (Held et al., 2010; Piwko et al., 2010; Santos et al., 2015; Zerjatke et al., 2017; Leonhardt et al., 2000; Leung et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Cells in the G1 phase of the cell cycle have been shown to decrease the levels of Pcna within the nucleus over time.
source: Cells in the G1 phase of the cell cycle have been shown to decrease the levels of Pcna within the nucleus over time (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Video 11, n = 9 epithelial cells) (Zerjatke et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data and citation to prior work.

claim: Cells progressing through to S phase have been shown to increase the levels of Pcna expression within the nucleus over time.
source: On the other hand, cells progressing through to S phase have been shown to increase the levels of Pcna expression within the nucleus over time (Leonhardt et al., 2000; Piwko et al., 2010; Leung et al., 2011; Santos et al., 2015; Barr et al., 2016; Zerjatke et al., 2017; Held et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: All tracked epithelial cells that eventually underwent a cellular division showed an increase in nuclear intensity of mScarlet-Pcna prior to the appearance of nuclear speckles.
source: Indeed, we found that all tracked epithelial cells that eventually underwent a cellular division showed an increase in nuclear intensity of mScarlet-Pcna prior to the appearance of nuclear speckles (Figure 4A–B'', Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Video 12, n = 9 epithelial cells).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: Nuclear speckles of Pcna mark the presence of replication foci in late S phase of the cell cycle.
source: Nuclear speckles of Pcna mark the presence of replication foci in late S phase of the cell cycle (Leonhardt et al., 2000; Piwko et al., 2010; Leung et al., 2011; Barr et al., 2016; Zerjatke et al., 2017; Held et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The S/G2 transition can be identified as the point of peak pixel intensity distribution of endogenous Pcna within the nucleus.
source: Previous work has also shown that the S/G2 transition can be identified as the point of peak pixel intensity distribution of endogenous Pcna within the nucleus (Zerjatke et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The peak pixel intensity distribution within nuclei was determined by a combination of 3D surface plots and histograms of pixel intensity distributions over time.
source: We were are able to determine the peak pixel intensity distribution within nuclei by a combination of 3D surface plots and histograms of pixel intensity distributions over time (Figure 4B–D, Figure 4—figure supplements 2 and 3, and Videos 12–14, n = 9 epithelial cells).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in figures and videos.

claim: Onset of M phase is marked by a sharp decrease in nuclear levels of Pcna.
source: Finally, onset of M phase is marked by a sharp decrease in nuclear levels of Pcna (Zerjatke et al., 2017; Leung et al., 2011; Piwko et al., 2010; Held et al., 2010), which we could consistently detect in the endogenous mScarlet-Pcna intensity tracks of epithelial cells undergoing division (Figure 4A–C, Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2, and Videos 12–14, n = 9 epithelial cells).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data and citations to prior work.

claim: The mScarlet-pcna line recapitulates known dynamics of Pcna within the nucleus and can be utilized as an endogenous 'all-in one' cell cycle reporter in vertebrates.
source: We therefore provide initial evidence that the mScarlet-pcna line recapitulates known dynamics of Pcna within the nucleus (Held et al., 2010; Piwko et al., 2010; Santos et al., 2015; Zerjatke et al., 2017; Barr et al., 2016; Leonhardt et al., 2000; Leung et al., 2011) and that it can therefore be utilized as an endogenous 'all-in one' cell cycle reporter in vertebrates.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the characterization data and citations to prior work.

claim: There is still a paucity of precise, single-copy fusion protein lines in vertebrates, in general, and in teleost fish in particular.
source: Despite the CRISPR/Cas9 system being repurposed as a broad utility genome editing tool almost a decade ago (Jinek et al., 2012; Cong et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2016) and despite its revolutionary impact as a method to generate knock-ins by HDR (Danner et al., 2017; Jasin and Haber, 2016; Ceccaldi et al., 2016; Lisby and Rothstein, 2004), there is still a paucity of precise, single-copy fusion protein lines in vertebrates, in general, and in teleost fish in particular.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of the field supported by citations.

claim: In medaka there are a total of three validated single-copy fusion protein lines by CRISPR/Cas9 reported prior to this work.
source: In fact, in medaka there are a total of three validated single-copy fusion protein lines by CRISPR/Cas9 reported prior to this work (Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018), and in zebrafish, a handful of lines have been reported so far (Wierson et al., 2020; Hisano et al., 2015; Auer et al., 2014; Kimura et al., 2014; Li et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The limited number of validated lines underscores the complexity of generating and validating precise single-copy fusion protein KI lines in teleost models.
source: This underscores the complexity of generating and validating precise single-copy fusion protein KI lines in teleost models.
evidence: This is an inference based on the paucity of lines.

claim: Previous techniques to generate large KIs required the usage of plasmid vectors commonly containing long homology arms (>200 bp).
source: Previous techniques to generate large KIs (such as fluorescent reporters) required the usage of plasmid vectors commonly containing long homology arms (>200 bp) (Zu et al., 2013; Shin et al., 2014; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Kimura et al., 2014; Li et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Problems arising during and after injection include DNA concatemerization of the donor construct.
source: Problems arising during and after injection include DNA concatemerization of the donor construct (Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018; Auer et al., 2014; Winkler et al., 1991; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Shin et al., 2014), in addition to possible imprecise and off-target integration of either the fluorescent protein sequence or the plasmid backbone (Auer et al., 2014; Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018; Won and Dawid, 2017; Wierson et al., 2020; Shin et al., 2014; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Kimura et al., 2014; Li et al., 2019; Yan et al., 2013; Hackett et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work documenting these issues.

claim: The vast majority of reported HDR-mediated knock-ins in teleosts rely on in vivo linearization of the plasmid donors.
source: The vast majority of reported HDR-mediated knock-ins in teleosts rely on in vivo linearization of the plasmid donors.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of the field.

claim: Linear dsDNA donors can drive HDR but might be prone to degradation, concatemerization, and are generally thought to be more toxic than plasmid donors.
source: This strategy is utilized due to the observation that, although linear dsDNA donors can drive HDR, they might be prone to degradation, concatemerization, and are generally thought to be more toxic than plasmid donors (Auer et al., 2014; Cristea et al., 2013; Auer and Del Bene, 2014; Hisano et al., 2015; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Wierson et al., 2020; Yao et al., 2017; Winkler et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Plasmid donors contain an additional guide RNA sequence to drive in vivo linearization in order to synchronize the availability of the linear DNA donor with Cas9 activity.
source: Plasmid donors therefore contain an additional guide RNA sequence to drive in vivo linearization in order to synchronize the availability of the linear DNA donor with Cas9 activity (Auer et al., 2014; Cristea et al., 2013; Hisano et al., 2015; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Kimura et al., 2014; Li et al., 2019; Wierson et al., 2020; Yao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Directly injecting PCR-amplified linear DNA with short homology arms (~35 bp) could be highly effective since these donors are relatively small (~780 bp) compared to plasmids (several kbs), and therefore a small quantity of donors (~10 ng/µl) will provide a large number of molecules (~20 nM) available to engage the HDR machinery following the Cas9-induced DSB.
source: We reasoned that directly injecting PCR-amplified linear DNA with short homology arms (~35 bp) could be highly effective since these donors are relatively small (~780 bp) compared to plasmids (several kbs), and therefore a small quantity of donors (~10 ng/µl) will provide a large number of molecules (~20 nM) available to engage the HDR machinery following the Cas9-induced DSB.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on molecular considerations.

claim: 5′ biotinylated primers were used in order to limit in vivo concatemerization of the donor construct.
source: Building on recent improvements in CRISPR/Cas9 KI strategies, we used 5′ biotinylated primers in order to limit in vivo concatemerization of the donor construct (Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018), and synthetic sgRNAs were used to increase the efficiency of DSBs by Cas9 (Paix et al., 2015; Kroll et al., 2021; Hoshijima et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a methodological detail supported by citation.

claim: Synthetic sgRNAs were used to increase the efficiency of DSBs by Cas9.
source: Building on recent improvements in CRISPR/Cas9 KI strategies, we used 5′ biotinylated primers in order to limit in vivo concatemerization of the donor construct (Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018), and synthetic sgRNAs were used to increase the efficiency of DSBs by Cas9 (Paix et al., 2015; Kroll et al., 2021; Hoshijima et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a methodological detail supported by citations.

claim: A monomeric streptavidin-tagged Cas9 was utilized that has a high affinity to the biotinylated donor fragments to increase targeting efficiency.
source: In addition, we utilized a monomeric streptavidin-tagged Cas9 that has a high affinity to the biotinylated donor fragments to increase targeting efficiency (Gu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a methodological detail supported by citation.

claim: The benefit of using the mSA/Biotin system to increase targeting efficiency in F0 needs to be further evaluated.
source: While 7/8 KI lines were generated and validated using Cas9 mSA and 5′ biotinylated donor fragments, the benefit of using the mSA/Biotin system to increase targeting efficiency in F0 needs to be further evaluated: in our initial comparison, using (2xNLS) Cas9 with and without mSA, and repair donors with and without biotinylation, we have found a comparable lethality and mosaic KI efficiency rates in F0s (Supplementary file 3g).
evidence: This is based on experimental comparison data.

claim: Cas9 containing only one NLS and no mSA showed a lower lethality rate and a lower mosaic KI efficiency in F0s compared to Cas9 with two NLSs.
source: We also tested another Cas9 containing only one NLS and no mSA (Gagnon et al., 2014) and found a lower lethality rate and a lower mosaic KI efficiency in F0s compared to Cas9 with two NLSs (Supplementary file 3g).
evidence: This is supported by experimental comparison data.

claim: The approach reported is a highly efficient, precise, and scalable strategy for generating single-copy fusion proteins.
source: Irrespective of these considerations, the approach reported here is a highly efficient, precise, and scalable strategy for generating single-copy fusion proteins (Supplementary files 3g and 4).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data.

claim: The fact that the repair donors are synthesized by PCR amplification eliminates the need for both cloning and a second guide RNA for in vivo linearization.
source: The fact that the repair donors are synthesized by PCR amplification eliminates the need for both cloning and a second guide RNA for in vivo linearization.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the methodology.

claim: The strategy significantly simplifies the process of endogenous protein tagging in a vertebrate model.
source: Therefore, the strategy we utilize significantly simplifies the process of endogenous protein tagging in a vertebrate model.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the methodological advantages.

claim: A similar approach to the one presented showed the potential to generate CRISPR/Cas9-mediated KI lines in zebrafish by targeting non-coding genomic regions with PCR-amplified donor constructs.
source: Very recently a similar approach to the one we present here showed the potential to generate CRISPR/Cas9-mediated KI lines in zebrafish by targeting non-coding genomic regions with PCR-amplified donor constructs (Levic et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to recent work.

claim: The work in zebrafish together with the present work in Medaka supports the notion that donors with short homology arms are sufficient to drive HDR when they are in the form of linear dsDNA.
source: Together with our present work in Medaka, this supports the notion that donors with short homology arms are sufficient to drive HDR when they are in the form of linear dsDNA.
evidence: This is an inference based on the current work and recent zebrafish work.

claim: Following the Cas9-induced DSB, the donor may be integrated by synthesis-dependent strand annealing (SDSA).
source: One possible explanation is that following the Cas9-induced DSB, the donor is integrated by synthesis-dependent strand annealing (SDSA).
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the mechanism.

claim: During SDSA, the 3′ ends of chromosomal DNA strands at the DSB can anneal with the repair donor and drive its replication and insertion at the site of the DSB.
source: During SDSA, the 3′ ends of chromosomal DNA strands at the DSB can anneal with the repair donor and drive its replication and insertion at the site of the DSB (Lisby and Rothstein, 2004; Danner et al., 2017; Jasin and Haber, 2016; Ceccaldi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on SDSA mechanisms.

claim: Short homologies (30–40 bp) appear to be sufficient to anneal with chromosomal DNA and engage the SDSA machinery.
source: Short homologies (30–40 bp) appear to be sufficient to anneal with chromosomal DNA and engage the SDSA machinery (Paix et al., 2017a, Paix et al., 2016; Grzesiuk and Carroll, 1987).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The validation process of single-copy insertions is complicated in approaches that use long homology arms (>200 bps) to generate knock-ins as concatemerization and the formation of episomes cannot be easily ruled out.
source: An important aspect of any KI strategy to generate fusion proteins is its precision. The validation process of single-copy insertions is complicated in approaches that use long homology arms (>200 bps) to generate knock-ins as concatemerization (Winkler et al., 1991; Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018) and the formation of episomes (Aljohani et al., 2020; Wade-Martins et al., 1999; Udvadia and Linney, 2003; Winkler et al., 1991; Wierson et al., 2020) cannot be easily ruled out.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work documenting these issues.

claim: Locus genotyping by PCR and Sanger sequencing is difficult when using primers external to the repair donor due to the large size of the expected fragment and competition for amplification with the wildtype allele.
source: Locus genotyping by PCR and Sanger sequencing is difficult when using primers external to the repair donor due to the large size of the expected fragment and competition for amplification with the wildtype allele.
evidence: This describes a technical challenge with long homology arms.

claim: Internal primers within the donor (junction PCR) have been used to avoid the limitation of large fragment size, but this can lead to PCR artefacts and crucially, it does not rule out concatemerization of the injected dsDNA.
source: Internal primers within the donor (junction PCR) have been used to avoid this limitation, but this can lead to PCR artefacts and crucially, it does not rule out concatemerization of the injected dsDNA (Won and Dawid, 2017; Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018; Auer et al., 2014; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Shin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Southern blotting is considered the gold standard to assess single-copy integration.
source: Southern blotting is considered the gold standard to assess single-copy integration (Wierson et al., 2020; Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018; Won and Dawid, 2017; Auer et al., 2014; Shin et al., 2014; Zu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Southern blotting depends on experimental design and probe design/sensitivity, and therefore cannot exclude that part of the donor construct or part of the vector backbone integrates elsewhere in the genome.
source: While it has its advantages, Southern blotting depends on experimental design (genomic DNA preparation and digestion strategy) and probe design/sensitivity, and therefore cannot exclude that part of the donor construct or part of the vector backbone integrates elsewhere in the genome.
evidence: This describes limitations of Southern blotting.

claim: It has been reported that plasmid donors can lead to additional unwanted insertions in the genome.
source: Indeed, it has been reported that plasmid donors can lead to additional unwanted insertions in the genome (Won and Dawid, 2017; Auer et al., 2014; Hoshijima et al., 2016; Kimura et al., 2014; Li et al., 2019; Shin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: WGS with high coverage on KI lines provides evidence that the approach yields single-copy integration only at the desired locus.
source: We address those issues by performing WGS with high coverage on KI lines and provide evidence that our approach yields single-copy integration only at the desired locus.
evidence: This is supported by WGS data.

claim: Utilizing repair donors with short homology arms on both ends (30–40 bp) simplifies the validation of the insertion by using primers that sit outside the targeting donor fragment.
source: In addition, utilizing repair donors with short homology arms on both ends (30–40 bp) simplifies the validation of the insertion by using primers that sit outside the targeting donor fragment.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the methodology.

claim: External primers can be used for genotyping of the full insertion by simple PCR followed by Sanger sequencing to know the precise nature of the edit.
source: These external primers can then be used for genotyping of the full insertion by simple PCR followed by Sanger sequencing to know the precise nature of the edit.
evidence: This describes the validation approach.

claim: The usage of donor fragments with short homology arms, in combination with high coverage WGS, are important aspects in validating the precision of single-copy CRISPR/Cas9-mediated KI lines in vertebrate models.
source: We show that the usage of donor fragments with short homology arms, in combination with high coverage WGS, to be important aspects in validating the precision of single-copy CRISPR/Cas9-mediated KI lines in vertebrate models.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the validation approach.

claim: Eight novel endogenous protein fusion lines were generated that significantly expand the repertoire of genetic tools to track cellular dynamics in medaka.
source: We were able to generate eight novel endogenous protein fusion lines that significantly expand the repertoire of genetic tools to track cellular dynamics in medaka.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental results.

claim: The generation of truly ubiquitous lines by transgene overexpression in teleost fish is a difficult endeavour and requires constant monitoring for variegation and silencing.
source: The generation of truly ubiquitous lines by transgene overexpression in teleost fish (Centanin et al., 2014; Burket et al., 2008) is a difficult endeavour and requires constant monitoring for variegation and silencing (Goll et al., 2009; Akitake et al., 2011; Burket et al., 2008; Stuart et al., 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Ubiquitous fluorescent reporter lines are invaluable tools for researchers.
source: Yet these ubiquitous fluorescent reporter lines are invaluable tools for researchers.
evidence: This is a general statement about the utility of such lines.

claim: Ubiquitous fusion proteins expressed from the endogenous locus avoid potential issues with transgene overexpression and variegation.
source: Ubiquitous fusion proteins expressed from the endogenous locus avoid potential issues with transgene overexpression and variegation.
evidence: This is an inference about the advantages of endogenous tagging.

claim: The highly conserved cbx1b locus could provide an alternative strategy to generate faithful ubiquitous nuclear markers in other teleosts and non-model organisms.
source: The highly conserved cbx1b locus could therefore provide an alternative strategy to generate faithful ubiquitous nuclear markers in other teleosts and non-model organisms.
evidence: This is a speculation about potential applications.

claim: The cbx1b locus could serve as a landing site for ubiquitous expression of genetic constructs in medaka.
source: In addition, this locus could serve as a landing site for ubiquitous expression of genetic constructs (e.g. utilizing a 2A self-cleaving peptide) in medaka (Li et al., 2019; Kim et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a speculation about potential applications supported by citations.

claim: The g3bp1-eGFP line can be used both as an in vivo marker of stress conditions and to study the process of stress granule formation.
source: This line can therefore be used both as an in vivo marker of stress conditions and to study the process of stress granule formation.
evidence: This is an inference about the utility of the line.

claim: Both neuromasts and the spinal cord show substantially higher expression of rab11a than other tissues.
source: We report that both neuromasts and the spinal cord show substantially higher expression of rab11a than other tissues, the basis of this remains unclear but could indicate that these tissues exhibit higher levels of protein turnover.
evidence: This is based on imaging data and speculation about the mechanism.

claim: No endogenous KI of any myosin family member has been reported in teleosts.
source: Despite being a highly conserved protein involved in myogenesis (Sellers, 2000; Hartman and Spudich, 2012), no endogenous KI of any myosin family member has been reported in teleosts.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of the field.

claim: N-cadherin has been shown to be involved in epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT).
source: Since N-cadherin has been shown to be involved in epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) (Harrington et al., 2007; Suzuki and Takeichi, 2008; Desclozeaux et al., 2008), this line can be used to study dynamical changes in N-cadherin distribution in vivo facilitating our understanding of EMT and other fundamental cell adhesion processes in vertebrates.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The cdh2-eGFP line can be used to study dynamical changes in N-cadherin distribution in vivo facilitating understanding of EMT and other fundamental cell adhesion processes in vertebrates.
source: Since N-cadherin has been shown to be involved in epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) (Harrington et al., 2007; Suzuki and Takeichi, 2008; Desclozeaux et al., 2008), this line can be used to study dynamical changes in N-cadherin distribution in vivo facilitating our understanding of EMT and other fundamental cell adhesion processes in vertebrates.
evidence: This is an inference about the utility of the line.

claim: An overarching goal of developmental and stem cell biology is to discover the location of stem and progenitor cells in different organs and tissues, followed by a molecular characterization of their properties.
